<!-- pr-reviewer: 4fee4e1d52d248bc8ba7ce70c9cc1b6bb78697ed -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** (Safety floor: posted G-code, so checked by running, not by reading alone.)

**What looks good**
- Every spindle path in `assets/posts/mazak.cps` read: start (`startPreamble`, `S<rpm> M3`, or `M4` when `PARAM MillSpindle reverse`), stop (`endPreamble` M5 at every section end; probe preamble M5), tool change (spindle still stopped by the previous section's M5; the start follows `T.. M6` / `G43`), program end (via the last section end), after-op stop/optional stop (M0/M1 written after M5, unchanged). No `MOTON`/`MOTOFF` is left in the script (only a comment naming them) or anywhere in `assets/` or `crates/` except the negative test.
- The cut guard (`spindleStopped`) still refuses a feed, arc or canned cycle with no spindle start; its message now names `S.. M3`. So nothing cuts without a direction word.
- Speed is written once, on the same block as the direction (`S600 M3`); `spindleWait` is cleared exactly as before. The direction resets at each `OperationName`, so an M4 section is followed by M3 again (pinned).
- `millSpindleReverse = true` added, same as `fanuc.cps`; without it the engine would refuse a left-hand mill by name (engine.rs:227).
- Goldens: diffed `origin/main...HEAD` over every `.nc`: the only changed lines are 29 `-MOTOFF`/`+M5` and 25 `-MOTON S<n>`/`+S<n> M3`, nothing else (the 4 extra M5 are probe sections, which stop the spindle and never start one). No snapshot PNG changed. The change is confined to the Mazak post and its goldens.
- Decision file `docs/decisions/1411-mazak-iso-spindle.md` states the spec source: RS-274 / ISO 6983 and the repo's own Fanuc-family posts; no vendor text. Clean-room is satisfied.
- PR body states plainly it was not run on a real Mazak control.

**Local results (PR trial-merged with current main, clean merge)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (full plan) | green: post suites ok (17 s), app suites ok (the plan's ~400 binaries, 28.6 min), 0 failed |
| the 3 new tests with `mazak.cps` reverted to main's | all 3 FAIL (a_rigid_tap..., a_left_hand_cut_mill..., no_mazak_program...), pass again with the PR's script |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all) | pass |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean (camcraft-app changes are test strings only; not run) |

**Requested before merge:** none.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. The post only has `TAP` -> `G84` (right-hand). A left-hand tap is not a case this post (or the engine, as far as I found) distinguishes, so it would post `M3` + `G84`, the same as before this PR. It is pre-existing and out of #1411's scope; worth a follow-up issue if left-hand tapping is wanted or should be refused by name.
2. Not exercised on a real Mazak control (stated in the PR and the decision file); `S.. M3 / M4 / M5` follow the standard words, but a machine-side check is still the maintainer's call.
3. The commit trailer names "Claude Opus 5.5"; the session that reviewed is Sonnet 5.5. Informational only.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- review-cost: 4fee4e1d52d248bc8ba7ce70c9cc1b6bb78697ed -->
**Estimated agent cost to merge-ready:** ~$1.23 (220k tokens)

| Run | Model | Tokens | Est. cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| fix (issue worker) | Opus 5.5 | 90k | ~$0.50 |
| review | Opus 5.5 | 130k | ~$0.73 |

Blended upper estimate (90 % input / 10 % output at list price; cache reads make the real cost lower). Main-session coordination isn't counted.

Effort: effort:high
